The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}+1}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $z,$ then $y,$ and then $x.$

activity_context.topic_title: Changing the Order of Integration in Triple Integrals: Changing Projection

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/024df0fe0a965feba2177adfac8bbd658fc90f4775a4707f13eba1ef2cb94702.png)

The triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over the region $R$ (shown above) can be expressed as the following repeated integral:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{z}}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

Rewrite this repeated integral by integrating first with respect to $x,$ then $z,$ and then $y.$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the given repeated integral, we see that $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z},\,\,1+y-z\le x\le 2}
$$

We wish to rewrite our triple integral as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Since both repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(y)}^{{v}_{2}(y)}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y
$$

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/8fff232443e6da697862c2e85a9d3abfe0554b80c2fcbfa8c93de42b94a45691.png)

The region $D$ is a type II region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 1,\,\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{z}}
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y,$ we write $D$ as a type I region.

Notice that the bottom boundary of the region, written in the form $z=z(y),$ is 

$$
y=\sqrt[3]{z}\,⟹\,z={y}^{3}
$$

and the top boundary of the region is

$$
z=1.
$$

Then, the type I representation of the region $D$ is

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,{y}^{3}\le z\le 1},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072974/assets/726ff420cae25c40f212714141a134fab84633cca7f49bdd268f0668d5248766.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{y}^{3}}^{1}{\int }_{1+y-z}^{2}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.
$$
